messages:
anya: Quick sync — I'm drafting an "initiative backing" doc for Optimize Toolkit. Customer asks keep eval-triggered alerts and quantization recommendations in the first delivery. Need a short list of launch gates and tradeoffs.

mike: curious which customers are pushing hard here?

anya: AcmeHealth and Inboxly flagged eval-alerts as critical for pilot acceptance. AcmeHealth also wants quant recs because they have strict latency/cost targets. Inboxly cares more about targeted alerting tied to prompt suites.

sanjay: From infra POV, eval-triggered alerts add signal plumbing but not huge infra load. Quant recs require running lightweight profiling jobs per model+workload — that is more ops.

claire: Product question — are we treating quantization recommendations as prescriptive ("do this quant config") or advisory ("here's what we saw; you can apply")? That affects rollout risk.

anya: Proposal: Phase 1 = advisory quant recs + basic eval-triggered alerts (threshold-based, templated). Phase 2 = auto-apply quant profiles and advanced alerts (signal scoring, auto-ack). Thoughts?

ben: +1 on advisory for launch. Also we should define SLOs: alert precision > 80% on our eval set, false-positive rate < 10% for pilot customers.

mike: Tradeoffs to call out in doc:
- Latency: aggressive quantization reduces latency but may regress quality.
- Cost: profiling jobs add transient cost; we can sample 1% of traffic to reduce cost.
- Reliability: eval alerts depend on stable eval harness and prompt sets — weight maintenance effort.

anya: Adding rough acceptance criteria block — please quick review:
```
AC-1: Eval-alerts sent for failing prompt sets within 15 min of detection, with triage link and failing examples.
AC-2: Quantization advisor provides recommended top-2 configs with estimated latency/cost delta and sample output diffs.
AC-3: Pilot customers can opt-in per-model; recommendations never auto-apply in phase 1.
AC-4: Latency regression alerting: if quant config increases median latency by >10% on pilot workload, flag immediate rollback suggestion.
```

sanjay: AC-2 requires a small profiling harness — I suggest we limit to 500 samples per model per run to keep runtime bounded.

claire: For launch gating, propose:
- Gate A: Signing customers for pilot (AcmeHealth + Inboxly) agree to opt-in and provide prompt suites.
- Gate B: Profiling harness deployed on dedicated infra with cost cap.
- Gate C: On-call runbook and alert playbook ready.

ben: Can we add a metric for "business impact amplification"? e.g., expected token-cost savings > X% or latency reduction > Y ms for 2/3 pilot customers. Helps prioritization vs other toolkit features.

anya: Good idea. I'll add an econ threshold: expected unit-cost reduction >= 12% or p95 latency drop >= 80ms for pilot tier. If neither met, deprioritize auto-apply flows to phase 2.

mike: One more item — UX for recommendations. We need a compact diff view (side-by-side sample outputs) and an "impact comb" showing cost/latency/quality tradeoffs. That affects scope a lot.

claire: UX MVP: list view with samples + quick accept/ignore. No in-console auto-apply in phase 1. Keep it minimal.

anya: Action items: 
- @sanjay: prototype profiling harness with 500-sample cap and cost estimate by EOD Tue.
- @mike: spec minimal diff UI (list view + sample diffs) by Wed.
- @ben: compute econ threshold numbers for AcmeHealth/Inboxly by Thu.
- @claire: draft pilot runbook + alert triage script.

deploy-bot: scheduled reminder set for 1765130000: "Toolkit initiative: prototype demos due" :bell:

anya: Thanks team. I'll fold these into the initiative backing doc and ping for final sign-off next week.
